title: Sephiria Costumes — All 27 Roster Skins, Effects & Unlocks (1.0)
description: Sephiria costumes guide: the full 27-skin roster with opening stat effects, the 19 unlockable skins and their conditions, and what sources disagree on.
meta: Covers sephiria costumes / costume unlocks / skin effects searches, including the salon unlock path and a sources-by-path table.
body:
Costumes change opening stats, not just looks. Align the skin with the weapon you plan to push.

How many costumes are there?

The launch listing says over 20 costumes. The community database we cross-checked tracks the roster at v1.0.24 and counts 27 playable costumes — 8 available from the start and 19 unlocked. Older guides list 17, which predates that roster. Values were rebalanced during 1.0, so treat the numbers below as a v1.0.24 community snapshot and check the skin in your own client.

The unlock path, in order

  1. Play runs and bank Sapphires. Sapphires come from dungeon depth and bosses defeated, so the currency arrives from ordinary play rather than a shop.
  2. Spend the first Sapphires on New Events. That branch opens town systems — the costume salon, the Wishing Fountain and extra weapons. See Destiny Inscription and the beginner guide.
  3. Open the salon before you pick a fight. Sources record the unlock through New Events but not the salon’s exact layout, so follow the prompt your client shows.
  4. Choose the costume before the floor. The choice happens pre-run, which is why it behaves like a loadout rather than a cosmetic.
  5. Check the effect in your own client. Values were rebalanced during 1.0, and every number on this page is a community snapshot.
  6. Chase task unlocks deliberately. Most unlockables below are counters, and some reset per run while others accumulate across runs. Read which before you grind.

Conditions the sources disagree on

CostumeReported unlocks

Listed in the v1.0.24 roster, unlock text not in the audited source

Scholar Lizard, Ghost, Otter, Eagle, Crocodile, Deer, Fairy of Fortune, Farmer Squirrel, Turtle, Forest Cat. Other skins in the roster are also unlocked by task-based play (for example grabbing a large number of Tablets in one run).

Two different counts: the 1.0.24 patch notes mention seven costumes receiving an additional purchasable appearance, which brought the appearance records to 79. Appearances are not playable costumes — do not add the two numbers together.

If a costume does not appear

  1. Confirm the version you are on. The roster count is taken at v1.0.24, and a guide listing 17 predates it, so the skin may be newer than the advice you are following.
  2. Check whether the counter resets per run. 333 damage and 10 Tablets are single-run conditions; the five-kill and five-donation conditions are not. Grinding the wrong type looks identical from the outside.
  3. Re-read the condition against your build. A run that never reaches 50 Fire damage cannot trigger Red-Clothed Cat, however many floors it clears.
  4. Check the cross-game unlock separately. Adventurer Rabbit asks for Dungreed on the same Steam account, and the guide author is not certain of it, so a missing skin there is not automatically a bug.
  5. Expect a conflict on Mole. Two guides say 300 fanatic moles and the wiki says the first boss, so verify in your client rather than trusting either count.
  6. Rule out a name mix-up. Seven costumes received an added purchasable appearance in 1.0.24, and appearance records reached 79. An appearance is not a playable costume.

Common mistakes

  • Adding appearances to the costume count. 27 playable skins and 79 appearance records describe different things and do not sum.
  • Treating a bonus as free. Every recorded effect is a trade, and Armored Rabbit pays for its defence with Max HP.
  • Picking the biggest number. The right skin props up the stat the build is worst at; a damage bonus on a run that dies to chip damage loses to a defence trade.
  • Reading silence as zero. Three starting costumes have no effect in the audited source, which is a gap in the record rather than a stat of nothing.
  • Planning from an older table. 1.0 rebalanced these values, so the client beats any list, including this one.

How to read these effects

Every row is a trade, not a straight upgrade: Armored Rabbit buys defence with Max HP, Orange Rabbit buys debuff damage with defence. Pick the costume that props up the stat your build is worst at, and see characters for what else changes between runs.

What this page does not cover

A costume is one decision among several before a run. Who the other characters are, and which NPC gates a weapon or a village event, is on characters; the route a costume should support is a build; the Sapphires that open both the salon and the fountain are a Destiny Inscription question; and the pre-run Artifact picks that pair with a costume are on Wishing Fountain.

Quick FAQ

Do costumes change stats or only looks?

Stats. Each one sets opening stats with a trade-off, which is why the roster reads like a loadout table rather than a skin gallery.

How do I open the costume salon?

Through New Events on the Destiny Inscription tree — the same early spend that unlocks the Wishing Fountain and extra weapons.

Why does my count differ from another guide?

Because the roster moved. Launch material says over 20 costumes, older guides list 17, and the v1.0.24 database counts 27 playable skins.

Is any costume strictly better?

No. Every recorded row trades something away, so the best pick depends on the stat your build is weakest at.

Can I change costume mid-run?

The costume is chosen before the floor, so a run is committed once you descend. No mid-run change is documented.
